prompt: What is the purpose of the Tripoli Unified Safety Code?

options.text: Establish guidelines for reasonably safe operation of rockets at a Tripoli launch
Establish guidelines for building of rockets at a Tripoli launch
Establish guidelines for the building of motors at a Tripoli launch

explanation: The Tripoli Unified Safety Code (TUSC) establishes guidelines for the reasonably safe operation of rockets at a Tripoli launch.

prompt: Although Tripoli launches involve several layers of safety rules intended to increase safety, _____ is ultimately responsible for the rocket and flight?

options.text: The Range safety officer
The launch Director
The flier

explanation: The flier is ultimately responsible for the rocket and the flight.

prompt: The flier shall document the location of the center of ____ and be able to demonstrate the center of _____ ? (Answer in order of blanks)

options.text: Gravity, Pressure
Pressure, Gravity
Pressure, Thrust

explanation: Document the center of pressure; demonstrate the center of gravity.

prompt: Which of the following motor types are not allowed to be made and flown by a Level 2 flier as a research motor?

options.text: Research Black Powder Motor
Liquid rocket motors (except nitrous oxide hybrids)
Both a. and b.

explanation: Neither research black powder motors nor liquid rocket motors (except N2O hybrids) may be made and flown by an L2 as research motors.

prompt: Rockets flown at Tripoli launches may carry:

options.text: Vertebrate Animals
Hazardous payloads including those which are poisonous, flammable, incendiary, or explosive
Neither a. nor b.

explanation: Neither vertebrate animals nor hazardous payloads.

prompt: What is the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ)?

options.text: The organization, office or individual responsible for enforcing requirements of a code or standard, or for approving equipment, materials, an installation or a procedure
A court proceeding that rule on high power rocketry activities
The individual preparing a high-power rocket for flight

explanation: The AHJ is the organization, office, or individual responsible for enforcing requirements of a code or standard.

prompt: What is a complex high-power rocket?

options.text: A rocket having more than one stage
A rocket having a cluster of rocket motors
Either a. or b.

explanation: A complex high-power rocket is either multi-stage or has a cluster of motors.

prompt: What are the minimum criteria that define a high-power rocket?

options.text: A rocket with a single motor with more than 160 Newton-seconds total impulse or an installed impulse of 320 Newton-seconds and no more than 40,960 Newton-seconds
A rocket with a single motor having an average thrust in excess of 80 Newtons or any sparky rocket motor (usually using titanium pieces)
Either a. or b.

explanation: Either condition defines a high-power rocket.
reference: TUSC 15 — Definition of High Power Rocket/Motor

prompt: What is the maximum weight of a model rocket with motors installed?

options.text: There is no maximum weight limit to a model rocket

explanation: 53 oz / 1500 g maximum with motors installed.

prompt: When is an active recovery device not necessary in a high-power rocket?

options.text: When the high-power rocket is intended for ballistic flight
When the rocket has a bursting charge
When the rocket employs a passive recovery system (e.g.: tumble recovery, aero-braking)

explanation: An active recovery device isn't required when a passive recovery system is used.

prompt: Range activity shall cease whenever a thunderstorm has been detected within ____ miles (kilometers) of the launch site?

options.text: 5 (8 kilometers)
10 (16 kilometers)
20 (32 kilometers)

explanation: 10 miles / 16 km.

prompt: At what total impulse and/or average thrust does a motor become high power?

options.text: A rocket motor with more than 80 Newton-seconds of total impulse and 80 Newtons average thrust
A rocket motor with more than 160 Newton-seconds of total impulse or 80 Newtons average thrust
A rocket motor with more than 160 Newton-seconds of total impulse and 160 Newtons average thrust

explanation: More than 160 N-s total impulse OR 80 N average thrust.
reference: TUSC 15 — Definition of High-Power Rocket Motor

prompt: While a 3:1 average thrust to weight ratio is the absolute minimum established in the Tripoli Unified Safety Code, what is the typical initial minimum thrust to weight ratio for a rocket?
explanation: 5:1 is the typical initial minimum thrust-to-weight ratio.

prompt: Who may operate a high-power rocket?

options.text: Any member of a nationally recognized rocketry organization
Only those licensed by the federal government
A certified user as defined in the Tripoli Unified Safety Code

explanation: A certified user as defined in the TUSC.
reference: TUSC 15 — Definition of High-Power Rocket Flier (HPR Flier)

prompt: What operating clearances must be complied with for flying high power rockets?

options.text: The Tripoli Unified Safety Code
The Tripoli Unified Safety Code, Regulations controlling airspace for country of launch and any other applicable federal, state and local regulations
NFPA and the FAA

explanation: TUSC plus airspace regulations and any other applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

prompt: What criteria apply to the construction of a high-power rocket?

options.text: Use suitable materials to withstand operating stresses and retain structural integrity in flight
Use only the lightest weight materials for the construction of high-power rockets
Use materials that allow minimal flex of the rocket in flight

explanation: Materials must withstand operating stresses and retain structural integrity.

prompt: When must the stability of a rocket be determined?

options.text: If the safety monitor requests it
During the design of the rocket
When the rocket is prepared for flight

explanation: Stability must be determined when the rocket is prepared for flight.

prompt: Who can override an RSO decision pertaining to safety?

options.text: RSO decisions pertaining to safety are final and may not be overridden by any other range personnel including the launch director
The Launch Director
A Tripoli BOD member, prefect, or TAP

explanation: RSO safety decisions are final.

prompt: When is it permissible to catch a high-power rocket?

options.text: If the rocket weighs less than 2.2 pounds or 1 kg
It is never permissible to catch a high-power rocket
If the rocket is falling slowly enough that it is deemed not to be a hazard

explanation: It is never permissible to catch a high-power rocket.

prompt: Except for pertaining to safety, who may override a launch directors' decision?

options.text: The LCO
A Tripoli BOD member, prefect or TAP
Except for pertaining to safety, the launch director's decision is final and cannot be overridden

explanation: Outside of safety, the LD's decision is final.

prompt: When must a high power rocket launching device incorporate a blast deflector?

options.text: When necessary to prevent damage or reduce risk of fire
All launch systems must incorporate a blast deflector
When the design of the launch device requires it

explanation: When necessary to prevent damage or reduce risk of fire.

prompt: What is the maximum launch angle from vertical for a high-power rocket?

options.text: There is no maximum launch angle

explanation: 20° maximum.

prompt: What are the elements of an ignition system?

options.text: Wireless controlled, electrically operated, a launch switch that returns to OFF when released
Wireless controlled, electrically operated and a removable safety interlock in series with the launch switch
Includes an arming switch with a removable key or interlock, which disables the entire launch control system when removed and uses a momentary switch to command the rocket motor ignition

explanation: Arming switch with removable key/interlock plus momentary firing switch.

prompt: When shall the motor ignitor(s) be installed in a high-power rocket motor?

options.text: At the launcher or a designated prep area
When the motor is installed in the rocket
Neither a. nor b.

explanation: At the launcher or a designated prep area.

prompt: When may the physical disconnects that inhibit energetics be connected to power?

options.text: In the flier Prep area
At the pad or other designated range area as indicated by the launch director
Both a. and b.

explanation: At the pad or other designated range area indicated by the launch director.

prompt: What is a class 1 rocket?

options.text: A model rocket with a G motor or smaller
A model rocket with more than 125 g (4.4 oz.) of propellant and more than 1500 g (53 oz.) pad weight
A model rocket with 125 g (4.4 oz.) or less of propellant and 1500 g (53 oz.) or less pad weight

explanation: Class 1 = model rocket: ≤125 g of propellant and ≤1500 g pad weight.

prompt: What is the launch site criteria?

options.text: No less than one-quarter the maximum altitude expected or granted by the FAA
No less than 1500 feet (457 m)
Both a. and b.

explanation: Both: at least 1/4 the max expected altitude AND at least 1500 ft.

prompt: What is the minimum distance from a launch site to any person or property not associated with the operation?

options.text: No minimum distance if the building occupants are informed of the activity.

prompt: How close can spectators be to a high-power rocket launch?

options.text: At the distance defined by the Safe Distances Table
Half the distance defined in the Safe Distance Table
Double the distance defined in the Safe Distance Table

explanation: At the distance defined by the Safe Distance Table.

prompt: What is the maximum altitude allowed for flying high power rockets if there is a cloud ceiling of 3,000 feet (914 m) and an FAA waiver to 15,000 feet (4572 m)?

options.text: Up to 15,000 feet (4572 m)
Up to 3,500 feet (1067 m)
Up to 3,000 feet (914 m)

explanation: Up to the cloud ceiling: 3,000 ft.

prompt: What is the limit of surface wind for launching a high-power rocket?

options.text: 30 MPH (48 km/h)
20 MPH (32 km/h)
15 MPH (24 km/h)

explanation: 20 MPH / 32 km/h.

prompt: When may a high-power rocket be launched?

options.text: After warning the spectators and after giving a 5 second countdown
When all systems are ready and after giving a 5 second countdown
After announcing the rocket and after giving a 5 second countdown

explanation: After announcing the rocket and giving a 5-second countdown.

prompt: What is a class 2 rocket?

options.text: A rocket other than a model rocket propelled by motors with greater than a combined total impulse of 640 N-s (143.9 lb-s)
A rocket other than a model rocket propelled by motors with greater than a combined total impulse of 40960 N-s (9208 lb-s)
A rocket other than a model rocket propelled by motors with less than a combined total impulse of 40960 N-s (9208 lb-s)

explanation: Class 2 = not a model rocket and propelled by motors with combined total impulse less than 40,960 N-s.
reference: TUSC 15 — Definition of High Power Rocket

prompt: What is the minimum distance for smoking (or open flames) from high power rocket motors, motor reloading kits and pyrotechnic modules?

options.text: 10 feet (3m)
25 feet (8m)
There is no minimum distance

explanation: 25 feet / 8 m.

prompt: When are you allowed to install an igniter or head end ignition module into any motor including a multistage, cluster or air start type rocket?

options.text: In the flier prep area
At the RSO table
At the pad or other designated area as established by the launch director

explanation: At the pad or designated area as established by the LD.

prompt: An R/C Rocket Boosted Glider (RBG) may be launched in which direction in regard to the flightline?

options.text: Parallel to or away from
Parallel to or towards
There is no direction requirement

explanation: Parallel to or away from the flightline.

prompt: At what impulse does a class 3 rocket start?

options.text: Above 5120 N-s (1151 lb-s)
Below 40960 N-s (9208 lb-s)
Above 40960 N-s (9208 lb-s)

explanation: Class 3 = above 40,960 N-s.

prompt: Test flights or first flights of R/C RBG shall be launched from the distance specified by the total installed impulse in the Safe Distance Table plus _____ Ft?
explanation: Plus 100 ft.

prompt: What is the maximum angle (in degrees) from vertical a model rocket can be launched from?
explanation: 30° from vertical for model rockets.

prompt: The minimum safe distance to any spectator when a model rocket is launched shall be _____ Ft?
explanation: 50 ft minimum.

prompt: The minimum distance for all involved rockets shall be the complex distance for the total installed impulse of the motors in all rockets when _____ or more rockets are launched simultaneously?
explanation: 3 or more rockets launched simultaneously.

prompt: When can steel nozzles be used in research motors?

options.text: When the nozzle throat is recessed within the case of a sugar motor
On any research motor
Never

explanation: When the nozzle throat is recessed within the case of a sugar motor.

prompt: What is the age limit Tripoli recognizes for a certified solid propellant high power rocket motor user?

options.text: 21 years of age
18 years of age
There is no age limit

explanation: 18 years of age.
reference: TUSC 15 — Definition of Adult flier, High Power Rocket Flier

prompt: What is the minimum safe distance for a non-complex H, I or J motor?
When may Research Motors that have been sold for a profit be used at a Tripoli Launch?

options.text: When the motors are not transported outside the state of manufacture
When the sale of motors is limited to certified users
It is never permitted

explanation: Never.

prompt: Which of the following materials can be used for research motor cases?

options.text: Metallic cases made of non-ferrous ductile metals such as 6061 aluminum alloy
Metallic cases made of ferrous metals such as Steel
Non-metallic cases made of PVC

explanation: Non-ferrous ductile metals like 6061 aluminum.

prompt: When is it permissible to consume alcohol when prepping or launching high power rockets?

options.text: When the preparation is done the day before the launch
If the blood alcohol level is below the "impaired" level
It is never permitted

explanation: Never.

prompt: Organizations that may certify high power rocket motors include:

options.text: Tripoli Rocketry Association (TRA) and the National Association of Rocketry (NAR) only
The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (BATFE)
TRA, NAR, and the Canadian Association of Rocketry (CAR)

explanation: NAR S&T, CAR MCC, and Tripoli TMT reciprocally recognize each other.

prompt: When can electronics that control energetics be powered on?

options.text: Before closing the rocket ebay in your campsite
After you have been through the rocket inspection
After the rocket is vertical on the pad but before the motor igniter is installed

explanation: After the rocket is vertical on the pad but before the motor igniter is installed.

prompt: The maximum landing speed of a rocket is not to exceed ____?

options.text: 15 ft/s (4 m/s)

prompt: Who in Tripoli may certify a member Level 1 or Level 2?

options.text: The prefect
A TAP member
A member of the Tripoli Board of Directors, the prefect, or a TAP member

explanation: BOD, prefect, or TAP member.

prompt: Who is allowed in the high-power launch area at a Tripoli launch?

options.text: Any invited person
Spectators
Tripoli TMP or Jr L1 NAR Members and any Tripoli or NAR member 18 years old or older

explanation: Tripoli TMP / Jr L1 NAR Members and any Tripoli or NAR member 18+.

prompt: When is electronically actuated recovery necessary?

options.text: There is no requirement, it is up to the flier
A high-powered rocket launched with an installed impulse greater than 2560 N-sec
A high-powered rocket launched with an installed impulse greater than 5120 N-sec

explanation: Required for installed impulse greater than 2560 N-s.
